title: Simon the Sorcerer wanted power without surrender.
paragraphs: Simon the Sorcerer wanted power without surrender.

He saw the miracles.
He watched the Holy Spirit move.
He stood close enough to the truth to feel its weight.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

You can be impressed by God
and still never bow to Him.

Simon believed in the spectacle.
He admired the authority.
He wanted the ability to lay hands on people and release what only God can give.
But his heart exposed him.

He did not want Jesus as Lord.
He wanted spiritual power as possession.
Read that again.

He wanted the gift,
without the Giver.
The influence,
without repentance.
The power,
without the cross.
That is still happening now.

People want anointing without holiness.
Authority without obedience.
Platform without brokenness.
Resurrection power without dying to self.
And that is where the danger begins.

Acts 8 does not show us a man merely confused.
It shows us a soul confronting the scandal of grace while still clutching the poison of pride.
Peter told him his heart was not right before God.
That is the real crisis.
Not weak branding.
Not delayed success.
Not lack of opportunity.
A heart out of alignment with God.

Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is the kind of warning many skip past too quickly.
You can start here:

Simon’s sin was not just greed.
It was rebellion dressed as reverence.

He was willing to stand near holy things,
as long as he did not have to die to himself.

And that is the sin beneath many polished Christian appearances.
A form of faith that wants benefits without surrender.
A language of God without the Lordship of Christ.
A fascination with miracles while refusing repentance.
But here’s the breaking point:

The Holy Spirit is not for sale.
The kingdom of God is not merchandise.
Grace cannot be bought.
Salvation cannot be earned.
And Jesus will never be reduced to a tool for human ambition.

This is why the gospel is not “try harder.”
It is not “clean yourself up.”
It is not “be spiritual enough.”

The gospel is this:
you are a sinner,
dead in sin,
unable to save yourself,
and no amount of religion, influence, or spiritual language can fix that.

But Jesus Christ came.
He lived the sinless life you could not live.
He died the death your sin deserved.
He rose again in victory.
And now forgiveness, redemption, and new life are given by grace through faith to those who repent and believe.

Not bought.
Not performed.
Received.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.

Maybe you have been near the things of God,
but not surrendered to the Son of God.
Maybe you have wanted His power,
but resisted His rule.
Maybe you have been building an image
while your heart remains untouched.

Then hear the mercy in the warning:
Repent.
Turn from sin.
Come to Christ.
He does not just expose false hearts.
He transforms them.

Don’t settle for proximity to power when Jesus offers new birth.
Don’t trade surrender for performance.
Don’t reach for the gift while rejecting the Savior.

Jesus is not your shortcut to significance.
He is Lord.
Follow the source. Go deeper with Gospel Warrior.

Are you seeking God…
or trying to use Him?
